subject: MedIQ on-prem integration: runway, constraints, cross-functional asks
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura@mediq.com>
To: priyom_das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Cc: infra@mediq.com
Date: 2026-08-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot: on-prem feasibility + network topology (MedIQ)

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the intro call earlier. As discussed, our security and compliance team is pushing for an on-prem (air-gapped) deployment of Redwood for a clinical inference workload. Attached is a first-draft SOW and our network topology diagram — we flagged three potential integration pain points:

- Egress limitations to external model registries
- KMS/HSM integration and key custody
- Audit-log retention requirements (7 years)

Can your team scope a quick feasibility review that covers: minimal infra footprint, required product exceptions, timeline to pilot, and an ops ownership model? We have a board milestone in Q4 and need a decision by mid-September on whether to pursue air-gapped.

Happy to hop on a 30-min sync next week.

Thanks,
Laura
Head of Infrastructure, MedIQ

Subject: Re: Pilot: on-prem feasibility + network topology (MedIQ)

Laura — thanks for the note and the files. Looping in infra (Soojin), product (Karthik), ops (Hannah) and CS (Jasmine) so we can do a quick cross-functional assessment.

Proposed agenda for internal review:
1) High-level compatibility: what parts of Redwood runtime need changes for air-gapped
2) Integration gating points (KMS, model registry, metrics/telemetry)
3) Minimal pilot infra + estimated engineering effort (weeks)
4) Ops/runbook and SLA expectations for pilot + handoff path to MedIQ
5) List of product exceptions/waivers required for the pilot

Soojin/Karthik/Hannah — can you each add a 1-paragraph summary and a rough estimate (low/med/high) of engineering effort by EOD Monday? I’ll synthesize and offer MedIQ a recommended pilot plan and a target decision date.

Laura — if you have specific compliance artifacts beyond the SOW (e.g., SOC2 scope, KMS vendor info), please drop them in the same thread.

— Priyom

From: soojin_lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
To: priyom_das <priyom@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, hannah_schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>, jasmine_liu <jasmine@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@mediq.com>
Date: 2026-08-31T08:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot: on-prem feasibility + network topology (MedIQ)

Quick infra readout after reviewing mediq-network-topology.png and the SOW:

Summary (Soojin): basic runtime can be containerized for an air-gapped environment, but several non-trivial items:
- Model artifacts: our typical flow pulls model weights from model registry (S3/HTTP). For air-gapped we need a supported offline model bundle workflow and a signed-bundle verification path.
- KMS/HSM: we can integrate with customer HSM via PKCS#11, but we will need a small shim and hardened key-rotation process. This requires security review and an engineer with crypto/HSM experience.
- Telemetry & observability: core telemetry can be forwarded to a local metrics stack, but our current tracing hooks assume outbound-agent to the Redwood control plane. We need a flag to disable outbound telemetry and an audit-log exporter that writes to local object storage with configurable retention.

Rough effort:
- Offline model bundle + verification: medium (4–6 wks, 1 engineer + 0.5 security)
- PKCS#11 HSM shim + rotation integration: medium-high (6–8 wks, 1 engineer + security lead)
- Local audit-log exporter & telemetry toggle: low-medium (2–3 wks, 1 engineer)

Open questions for MedIQ: what HSM vendor and access model? Is there an internal registry we should use for image hosting?

I recommend we scope a 6–8 week pilot if we get approvals and one named engineering owner from MedIQ. Attaching network diagram into our notes.

— Soojin
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: priyom_das <priyom@redwood.ai>, soojin_lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, hannah_schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>, jasmine_liu <jasmine@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@mediq.com>
Date: 2026-08-31T11:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot: on-prem feasibility + network topology (MedIQ)

Product notes and roadmap compatibility:

- Core runtime: supported. We already have customers running isolated instances but not full air-gapped with zero egress. The product gaps are primarily around: offline model bundle management (versioning + delta updates), and function-calling integrations that assume outbound webhooks.
- Minimal supported feature set for Pilot (recommendation): text generation, embeddings, and a single controlled webhook path for post-processing that can be proxied locally. No streaming for the initial pilot to reduce complexity.
- Exceptions we will likely ask product leadership for: 1) disable remote model telemetry for the pilot, 2) temporary waiver on automated model updates (manual pushes only), 3) an SLA carve-out for latency-sensitive workloads until we validate local infra.

Effort estimate (product + API): low-medium (3–5 wks) to implement config flags and bundle handling for pilot.

If Legal/Security needs a documented exception path, we should prepare a 1-page product limitations memo. Happy to draft.

— Karthik
Director, Product Management, Redwood Inference
From: hannah_schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
To: priyom_das <priyom@redwood.ai>, soojin_lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, jasmine_liu <jasmine@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@mediq.com>
Date: 2026-09-01T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot: on-prem feasibility + network topology (MedIQ)

Ops/Support view:

- Handoff model: we should run the pilot as 'Redwood-managed on-prem' for the initial 8 weeks, with a short transition plan to MedIQ ops. That keeps our engineers in the loop and avoids early outages.
- Oncall and SLA: for the pilot we'll provide a dedicated rotation (2 engineers) + a 4-hour P1 response target. For production handoff we'd need MedIQ to adopt our playbooks and accept a supported-oncall model; otherwise we must price the ongoing managed service.
- Runbooks & compliance artifacts needed: runbook for deployment, key custody procedures, audit-log access process. Hannah can produce templates but will need 2–3 days partner time to validate against MedIQ compliance.

Ops resourcing ask: one backend engineer (0.5 FTE for 8 weeks) for deployment + one SRE (0.25 FTE) to own telemetry/exporter work. Those are above the engineering estimates Soojin listed.

— Hannah
Head of Operations, Redwood Inference

Subject: MedIQ pilot recommendation and action items (decision requested by 2026-09-15)

Thanks everyone — summary and proposed next steps for MedIQ:

Summary: cross-functional review indicates pilot is feasible if MedIQ agrees to:
- Provide HSM vendor details and a named infra engineer for the pilot (required)
- Accept a constrained pilot feature set (no streaming; manual model update bundles)
- Sign a short SOW for 'Redwood-managed on-prem pilot' (8 weeks) with explicit handoff criteria

Estimated internal effort (consolidated): 6–8 weeks of coordinated work across infra/product/ops (soojin + karthik + hannah estimate), staffing: 1 backend engineer (0.5–1.0 FTE), 1 SRE (0.25 FTE), 1 security reviewer (part-time).

Action items (owners / due):
1) MedIQ: confirm HSM vendor + provide registry/image hosting details (Laura) — due 2026-09-10
2) Priyom: draft pilot SOW and product limitations memo (includes exception list) — due 2026-09-07
3) Soojin: prototype offline model-bundle checklist and required infra diagram updates — due 2026-09-14
4) Hannah: deliver runbook templates and P1/P2 targets for pilot support — due 2026-09-10
5) Karthik: draft 1-page product limitation memo for Legal/Security — due 2026-09-07

Laura — if you can confirm the HSM vendor and provide a preferred time for a 30-min alignment call (we're proposing 2026-09-08 or 2026-09-09), we will finalize the draft SOW and get this into Legal for an expedited review.
